samples.summary: The reply endpoint's Long→number timestamp conversion is never asserted
samples.evidence: `reply()` returns `{ threadId, comment: { ...reply, createdAt: Number(reply.createdAt) } }`. `buildReply` stores `createdAt` as a `bigint` (comment-ops.ts `toYorkieMs`), and `res.json()` throws on a BigInt, so this single `Number(...)` is what keeps every reply from becoming a 500. The only assertion any test makes about the reply response is `expect(reply.threadId).toBe(thread.id)` (comments.controller.spec.ts:219); grepping the spec for `createdAt` shows the only numeric assertion is on `threads[0].createdAt` from `list` (line 162), which goes through `copyThread`, a different conversion. Dropping or regressing the conversion in `reply` would leave the whole suite green while every reply request fails at serialization.
searchedFor: read comment-ops.spec.ts (covers copyThread/fromYorkieMs, not the reply route response)

samples.summary: 'keeps a concurrent edit to another slide' does not test granularity — it passes under a whole-array reassignment
samples.evidence: The test snapshots `slides()[0]` and a copy of its first element, calls `controller.add`, then asserts `expect(slides()[0]).toBe(untouched)` and element equality. No concurrent edit is ever made (the 'peerEdit' is just a pre-copy of existing data), and object identity is preserved by any implementation that reuses the same slide objects — including `root.slides = [...old, newSlide]`, which is exactly the last-write-wins pattern the comment says this guards against. The real granularity property is tested in slide-ops.spec.ts ('carries only the new slide, never a replacement deck' / 'reorders in place ... never rebuilding'), so this controller-level test contributes no signal while being presented as the reason the verbs exist.

samples.summary: The `to < from` in-place reorder branch of applySlideChange is untested
samples.evidence: `applySlideChange`'s move case has three proxy paths: `moveFront` (to===0), `moveAfterByIndex(to, from)` (to>from) and `moveAfterByIndex(to - 1, from)` (0<to<from). slide-ops.spec.ts 'reorders in place when the array offers it, never rebuilding' exercises only the first two (`expect(calls).toEqual(['moveFront:ticket-2', 'moveAfterByIndex:2:0'])`); every other move test uses a plain array and therefore the splice fallback. An off-by-one in the `to - 1` arm would land a mid-deck move on the wrong position with the suite green.

samples.summary: `withSref`'s orphaned-thread (`ref: null`) result has no test
samples.evidence: `withSref`'s docblock states the derived `ref` is `null` once the anchored row or column is deleted, and that this is 'exactly how the editor tells an orphaned thread from a live one' — i.e. a documented, consumer-visible field of the list response. Every test in comments.controller.spec.ts asserts live refs only ('A1', 'B2'); nothing deletes an axis id and re-lists. No test asserts a null `ref`.

samples.summary: Several new validation/refusal branches of the comments controller are untested
samples.evidence: Untested branches: (a) `createThread` on a sheet with an unknown `tabId` → `NotFoundException('Tab not found')` — the spec only uses 'tab-1'/'tab-2'; (b) the `parseRef` catch in `sheetCellAnchor` → 'Invalid cell reference' — the 'refuses a cell whose row or column has no id yet' test uses 'Z99', which parses fine and hits the other branch; (c) `parsePdfAnchor` with a non-object or partially-missing `rect` (only `w: 2` out-of-range is covered); (d) `notify`'s early return when the author's `userId` is not a positive integer (an anonymous share-link author), so no test proves such a comment silently skips notification rather than throwing.

samples.summary: `planCommentNotifications` is exported 'for its own test' but has no test file; two of its cases are uncovered
samples.evidence: Its docblock says 'Exported for its own test: this is the only part of the notification path that is a decision rather than a database write.' A repo-wide grep for `planCommentNotifications` finds only notify.ts / notify.test.ts (frontend) and comments.controller.ts — there is no backend test importing it. It is only exercised indirectly through the controller, and two decisions are uncovered there: a reply that mentions a NON-participant (should emit both a `comment_mention` and a `comment_reply` plan — every existing test yields exactly one plan), and a resolve whose only participant is the actor (should emit nothing).

samples.summary: No test covers the new board/comments registrations on the real buildProgram
samples.evidence: `registerBoardCommand` and `registerCommentsCommand` are added to `buildProgram()` in cli.ts, but class-b-commands.test.ts builds its own program (`createProgram()` + explicit registers) and namespaces.test.ts does the same. The only test over the real `buildProgram` is output.test.ts:922, which asserts `expect.arrayContaining([... 'docs','sheets','slides','notes','api-keys','schema'])` — 'board' and 'comments' are absent from that list, so removing either registration (making the commands unreachable from the shipped binary) leaves the suite green.

samples.summary: ~18 new schema registry entries have no test asserting their presence or agreement with the CLI tree
samples.evidence: The diff adds registry entries for slides.layouts, slides.slide.*, board.*, comments.* and sheets.tabs.delete/move/duplicate and sheets.images.*. schema.test.ts's 'canonical names are plural' lists only pre-existing names, and 'safety levels match the design contract' checks only pre-existing entries; the new alias-collision test is generic and would pass with none of the new entries present. Nothing asserts that a registry name corresponds to a real command or that e.g. comments.delete is classed 'destructive'.

samples.summary: CLI stdin payload path and several argument-validation paths are untested
samples.evidence: class-b-commands.test.ts drives `sheets images set` only via `--data`; the `for await (const chunk of process.stdin)` branch (and the 'Invalid JSON image data on stdin' message it produces) is never executed. Likewise for comments: `--page abc` (non-integer), `--page` given with no `--rect`, and `--rect` given with no `--page` all reach distinct error messages in comments.ts, and only the out-of-range rect case is tested.

samples.summary: duplicateTab's metadata carry-over and applyDelete's missing-worksheet path are untested
samples.evidence: `duplicateTab` conditionally copies `kind`, `datasourceId` and `query` onto the new `TabMeta`; tab-ops.spec.ts only duplicates a plain sheet tab (name uniquing, cells, comments dropped), so dropping any of those three fields would go unnoticed. Similarly `applyDelete` guards `if (root.sheets?.[tabId]) delete ...` for datasource/lakehouse tabs, but no test deletes a tab that has metadata and no worksheet.

samples.summary: `expect(result).not.toHaveProperty('slides')` is guaranteed by the type, not by behavior
samples.evidence: In 'carries only the new slide, never a replacement deck', `SlideOpResult` has no `slides` member at all, so this assertion can never fail for any implementation that type-checks. The adjacent `toMatchObject({ kind: 'insert' })` is the assertion doing the work.

samples.summary: PDF list/reply/resolve/delete paths are only covered for create
samples.evidence: comments.controller.spec.ts asserts `docKeyPrefix: 'pdf-'` for the create path only (`withDocument.mock.calls[0][2]`). The flat-root list/mutate paths are exercised with `type: 'doc'` fixtures; nothing checks that a PDF document reaches those paths with the pdf prefix, so a wrong `prefixFor` on the mutate paths would open the wrong Yorkie document undetected.
searchedFor: read comments.controller.spec.ts 'on a PDF' describe block

verdict.reason: Verified the evidence: comments.controller.ts:355 returns `createdAt: Number(reply.createdAt)` for the reply route, and buildReply (comment-ops.ts:172-187 via toYorkieMs at :58-60) genuinely produces a runtime bigint, typed as `number` so removing the cast still compiles. I read all 585 lines of comments.controller.spec.ts: every controller.reply() call (177, 212, 246, 371, 485, 518) either discards the result or asserts only `reply.threadId` (219); the sole numeric timestamp assertion (162) is on the `list`/copyThread path. I searched wide for a counterexample and found none: no backend e2e spec touches comments/reply (grep for `comment` in packages/backend/test hits only notification, revision-history, slides-pptx-import, document-copy-attached, none exercising reply); the only other reply caller is the CLI, whose test (packages/cli/test/class-b-commands.test.ts:320-333) mocks the HTTP client and asserts call args only, never a real response; repo-wide greps for `\.reply\(`, `replies`, `replyToComment`, `typeof .*createdAt`, `createdAt).toBe(`, `expect.any(Number)` surfaced nothing asserting the reply response's createdAt. Missing test over a path where failure means every reply request 500s at serialization = major under this lens.
